proof.text: First fix the completed tensor comparisons. For arbitrary ambient $V,W$ and complete $Z$, the closed tensor adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] identifies precomposition by $\eta_V\otimes1_W$ with precomposition by $\eta_V$ on maps into $R\mathcal Hom(W,Z)$. That last object is complete by [lem-sf-ringed-rhom-derived-complete], so the completion adjunction [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] makes this a bijection. Thus $C(\eta_V\otimes1_W):C(V\otimes W)\to C(CV\otimes W)$ is invertible: testing maps to its complete source and target gives a two-sided inverse. Symmetry gives the comparison for the other factor. The same hom-set argument gives $C_{\mathcal X}u^*(\eta_V)$ invertible, because maps into complete $Z$ transpose to maps into the complete object $PZ$. These comparisons specify the completed pullback tensor isomorphism. Their coherence follows by precomposing with the completion units: every resulting associativity or unit diagram becomes the ordinary tensor/pullback diagram, and these precompositions are injective. In the remaining steps all tensor signs without a hat denote ordinary derived tensor.

proof.text:
Put $M=PH\otimes K$ and $N=H\otimes u^*K$, so the required source and target are $C_{\mathcal Y}M$ and $PC_{\mathcal X}N$. Write $\varepsilon:u^*P\to1$ for the ordinary counit. By the induced hom-set bijections in [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], the completed counit $\varepsilon^c_H:C_{\mathcal X}u^*PH\to H$ satisfies $\varepsilon^c_H\eta_{u^*PH}=\varepsilon_H$. Under the unit-induced tensor comparisons of Step 1, the completed projection transpose, restricted along the units, is consequently
$$u^*(PH\otimes K)\cong u^*PH\otimes u^*K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_H\otimes1}N\xrightarrow{\eta_N}C_{\mathcal X}N.$$
Indeed its two tensor-factor units are followed by $\varepsilon^c_H$ and the identity of $C_{\mathcal X}u^*K$, respectively; the first cancels by the counit equation and the second gives $\eta_{u^*K}$. The definition of the comparison for the second factor in Step 1 then gives $\eta_N$. The ordinary projection has transpose $(\varepsilon_H\otimes1)\mu$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Transposing the displayed equality yields
$$\pi^c\eta_M=P(\eta_N)\pi^o.$$
Since $PC_{\mathcal X}N$ is complete, the completion adjunction makes precomposition with $\eta_M$ bijective. This also proves the asserted uniqueness.

proof.text: Let $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. On the small diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] use both the constant ring $\Delta\underline A_T$ and the ring sheaf $B_T=(\underline{A/I^n}_T)_n$. The latter is a sheaf: the sheaf condition is imposed separately at each index, and every horizontal map is the actual quotient homomorphism. Its modules are strict semilinear quotient systems; kernels and cokernels are computed componentwise, by their ordinary module universal properties. Restriction along $\Delta\underline A_T\to B_T$ is exact and reflects quasi-isomorphisms, since these properties are detected on underlying cohomology sheaves. Write $U_T$ for this restriction, $S_T=-\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T$, and $\mathcal R_T=S_T\Delta_T$. Let $\mathcal L_T$ be total derived inverse limit on constant-$A$ towers. Choose one flat-term K-flat representative $Q$ of an ambient object $V$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its diagonal is K-flat: tensor with an acyclic tower is acyclic at each index, hence acyclic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The tensor construction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] therefore represents $\mathcal R_TV$ by the actual strict tower $(Q\otimes_A\underline{A/I^n})_n$. Denote its underlying augmentation by $i_V:\Delta V\to U_T\mathcal R_TV$. This fixes quotient transitions before localization; it makes no choice of unrelated derived level maps.

proof.text: Use $G=u^*$ on constant-$A$ towers, $P^J=Ru_*^J$, and $G_B\dashv P_B$ on the $B$-ringed diagram sites. These adjunctions come from componentwise module adjunctions, whose hom-set bijections preserve transition squares by naturality. The derived adjunctions and their normalization are [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact, lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]. The constant tower functor $\Delta$ preserves K-injectives. To see this, $1$ is terminal in $J$, and a tower map $T\to\Delta V$ is uniquely determined by $T_1\to V$; hence $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta$ with exact left adjoint [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. K-injective resolutions exist on the small diagram sites [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. On a diagonal K-injective representative the literal identities $u_*^J\Delta=\Delta u_*$ and $\lim\Delta=1$ consequently give $P^J\Delta=\Delta P$ and $\mathcal L\Delta=1$, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The fraction formula for the derived adjunction identifies diagonal counits with the ordinary counit. Finally $\mathcal L_Ti_V=\eta_{T,V}$, by the completion formula and unit of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction].

Write $a_T$ as $a_V:P\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}P^JV$, using [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. We verify its counit normalization rather than infer it from projections. The exact adjunction $\Delta\dashv\lim$ derives to $\Delta\dashv\mathcal L$: use [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] and the K-injective computation of Step 4. The two composite derived adjunctions give the bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}P^JV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta M,P^JV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G\Delta M,V)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta u^*M,V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u^*M,\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,P\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V).$$
Their right-adjoint comparison is $a_V^{-1}$: before derivation both sides are the identical composite $u_*\lim=\lim u_*^J$; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the fraction normalization identify its derived comparison with the specified $a$. Thus, for a tower arrow $b:GZ\to V$, its tower adjunct $b^\sharp:Z\to P^JV$, and an augmentation $j:\Delta M\to Z$, the ordinary adjunct of the total-limit map of $b\,G(j)$ is exactly
$$a_V^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(b^\sharp)\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(j):M\to P\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}V.$$
Here $G\Delta M=\Delta u^*M$ and $\mathcal L\Delta=1$. This proves the stated transpose/augmentation compatibility for whole tower arrows, including their counits.

On the ringed diagram square formed by $u$ and the coefficient maps $\Delta\underline A\to B$, let
$$h_F:\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(PF)\longrightarrow P_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F$$
be the coefficient exchange mate, with transpose $S_{\mathcal X}\Delta(\varepsilon_F)$ under $G_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}\cong\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}u^*$. The coefficient restrictions identify $U_{\mathcal Y}P_B\cong P^JU_{\mathcal X}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], applied to the two factorizations of the same ringed morphism; restriction is exact. Under this comparison $U h_F$ is the constant-$A$ diagram projection for $\Delta F$ and coefficient diagram $B$. Indeed both transposes are counit tensor identity, with the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. The derived fraction formula [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] preserves this equality from the module adjunctions. Evaluation of this underlying projection is the ordinary projection with constant coefficient $\underline{A_n}$, by the evaluation comparison of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] and the pullback/tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. No flatness of $A\to A_n$ is asserted.

proof.text: For each $n$, take a bounded finite-projective $A$-complex representing $A_n$. Its constant sheaf complex still represents $\underline{A_n}$: the constant-module functor is inverse image from the point, so preserves kernels and cokernels. Every term retains its explicit retraction from a finite free sheaf. Apply [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows, lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization] to these packages on the ordinary ringed topoi. They say that the counit-defined evaluated map $h_{F,n}$ is invertible. Thus $h_F$ is invertible on the whole derived diagram: its underlying cone has zero cohomology at every index, so is zero by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; exact restriction reflects zero cohomology. These are the specified perfect-coefficient projection comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms. Since $h_F$ was constructed on the diagram, all its quotient transitions already commute. Notice that this uses perfectness of $A_n$ over $A$, but neither finite cardinality of $A_n$ nor a scheme hypothesis.

proof.text:
The scalar-extension tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], on the two diagram sites, gives
$$\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}M\cong\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(PH)\otimes_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}K,\qquad \mathcal R_{\mathcal X}N\cong\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}H\otimes_B G_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}K.$$
Let $\pi_B$ be the projection for $G_B\dashv P_B$ and set
$$v=\pi_B\circ(h_H\otimes1):\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}M\longrightarrow P_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}N.$$
This is a specified arrow on the $B$-ringed diagram site. Its evaluation is $\pi^{(n)}_{H_n,K_n}$ after the source comparison $h_{H,n}$ and tensor balancing. For clarity, evaluation is exact on the quotient systems because underlying kernels and cokernels are componentwise. Its direct-image comparison is obtained by restricting to the constant-$A$ tower, using the comparison in Step 6, then evaluating and using the same ringed-composition comparison at $A_n$. The fraction formula [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] identifies the evaluated adjunction with $u_n^*\dashv Ru_{*,A_n}$: the underlying module bijections are those of $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with the quotient action. Substitution in the counit-tensor transpose formula [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] gives exactly the stated finite mate. This argument does not assume that evaluation preserves K-injectives for varying coefficient rings.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the diagram-site ringed square with vertical maps $u$ over $A$ and $B$, horizontal coefficient-extension maps, object $\Delta H$, and tensor argument $\Delta K$. Its two composites are precisely $v$ of Step 8 and $h_N\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(\pi^o)$. The tensor identifications are the scalar-extension comparisons already fixed in Step 8, and the constant-diagram projection is $\Delta\pi^o$ by Step 4. Therefore
$$v=h_N\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(\pi^o)$$
in the derived category of $B$-module diagrams. This proves equality before restriction, inverse limit, or evaluation; it uses no faithfulness of any derived reduction functor.

proof.text:
Write $\widetilde h_F=U h_F$ under the direct-image comparison of Step 6, so $\widetilde h_F:U\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(PF)\to P^JU\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F$. Naturality in the coefficient argument and tensor-unit normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied on the constant-$A$ diagram sites to $\Delta\underline A\to B$, give
$$\widetilde h_F i_{PF}=P^J(i_F).$$
Indeed the projection for the tensor unit is the identity of $\Delta PF$, and the two vertical arrows of this naturality square are the actual quotient augmentations. Define
$$\rho_F=a_{U\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F}^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(\widetilde h_F):C_{\mathcal Y}PF\longrightarrow PC_{\mathcal X}F.$$
Apply $\mathcal L$ to the preceding square. Naturality of $a$ [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], $a_{\Delta F}=1$ on diagonal K-injective representatives, and $\mathcal L(i_F)=\eta_F$ from Step 4 yield
$$\rho_F\eta_{PF}=P(\eta_F).$$
This is the normalized unit equation for the specified whole-tower comparison; it is not deduced from equalities of evaluated arrows.

proof.text:
Take the total inverse limit of $Uv$ and then use $a^{-1}$ on its target. Its source is $\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}U\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}M=C_{\mathcal Y}M$, and its target is $PC_{\mathcal X}N$, by [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction, lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. Step 9 gives the formula $r=\rho_N C_{\mathcal Y}(\pi^o)$ for this total-limit arrow. Step 10 and naturality of $\eta$ give
$$r\eta_M=\rho_N\eta_{PN}\pi^o=P(\eta_N)\pi^o.$$
The uniqueness proved in Step 2 implies $r=\pi^c$. By Steps 7 and 8, this is exactly the total limit of the finite projection mates, with source identification given by the perfect-coefficient comparisons and balancing, and target identification given by $a^{-1}$. Step 5 proves that the same identifications preserve the counits and the transpose of any strict tower arrow after a constant augmentation. Every construction used is natural, so these are equalities of the specified natural transformations. This proves all clauses of the item.

title: Completion coherence for the integral projection mate
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subset A$ an ideal, and assume each $A_n=A/I^n$, $n\geq1$, is perfect over $A$ (a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules represents it). Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ be a morphism of topoi on small sites, with constant $A$-module sheaves and ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the exact inverse image $u^*$, its K-injective derived right adjoint $P=Ru_*$, and their canonical counit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. For $T=\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ use the completion reflector $C_T:D_T\to D_{T,\mathrm{comp}}$ with unit $\eta_T$ and $C_TV=R\lim_n(V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T)$, and the induced completed adjunction $u_c^*=C_{\mathcal X}u^*\dashv P$ [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. Write $V\widehat\otimes W=C_T(V\otimes_A^LW)$ on complete objects. For complete $H\in D_{\mathcal X}$ and $K\in D_{\mathcal Y}$, let
$$\pi^c_{H,K}:C_{\mathcal Y}(PH\otimes_A^LK)\longrightarrow P C_{\mathcal X}(H\otimes_A^Lu^*K)$$
be the projection mate for that completed adjunction and completed tensor. If $\pi^o_{H,K}:PH\otimes_A^LK\to P(H\otimes_A^Lu^*K)$ is the ordinary counit-defined projection, then
$$\pi^c_{H,K}\circ\eta_{\mathcal Y,PH\otimes_A^LK}=P(\eta_{\mathcal X,H\otimes_A^Lu^*K})\circ\pi^o_{H,K}.$$
This characterizes $\pi^c$ uniquely. It also identifies $\pi^c$ with the total derived inverse limit of the finite-quotient projection mates $\pi^{(n)}_{H_n,K_n}$, formed on the ringed diagram site, where $H_n=H\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}$ and $K_n=K\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}$ and the finite tensor is over $\underline{A_n}$. The source identification uses the canonical perfect-coefficient projection comparisons $(PH)_n\cong Ru_{*,A_n}H_n$ and tensor balancing; the target identification uses the canonical direct-image/total-limit comparison [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. All transitions are coefficient restrictions on one strict quotient diagram [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. The identification includes the counits: under these canonical direct-image/limit comparisons, the adjunction transpose of a strict tower map, composed with a constant-tower augmentation, equals the ordinary transpose of its limit map. It is equality of the specified transformations, without a faithfulness assumption on individual reductions.
